title: 中国人怎么吃一只鸡②白切鸡：最贵的一道鸡，什么都不加 | How China Eats a Chicken P2 · Cantonese White-Cut 🐔
description:
你吃白切鸡，蘸姜葱还是蘸生抽？

中国人怎么吃一只鸡 第②集 · 广东白切鸡。广东人一句「无鸡不成宴」，而宴上最讲究的那只鸡，偏偏什么都不加——不放酱料，只在清水（或高汤）里浸到刚熟，随吃随斩，所以又叫白斩鸡。它始于清代民间食肆；越是简单，越考火候：皮要爽、肉要滑、骨头带一点血丝才算到位，蘸的也只是姜葱、油盐。1981年广州清平饭店改用海味药材熬的卤水来浸，成了名店「清平鸡」。一只好鸡，自己就够鲜。

In Cantonese cooking, "no chicken, no feast" — and the feast's proudest chicken adds nothing at all. Bai qie ji (white-cut chicken) is simply poached in clear water or light stock until just cooked, then chopped to order. It appeared in Qing-dynasty eateries, and the plainer it looks, the harder it is: crisp skin, silky flesh, the timing judged to the minute, with only ginger-scallion oil to dip. In 1981 Guangzhou's Qingping restaurant poached theirs in a herb-and-seafood brine, creating the famous "Qingping chicken." A good chicken needs nothing more.
